hypothesis: With expert workers, every prefill chunk makes each worker read a layer's experts again from disk, so prefilling a 245-token prompt in one chunk instead of two nearly halves the workers' disk time and the prefill gets faster without changing any token.
model: GLM-5.3-Flash (a community abliterated fine-tune; same architecture and tensor shapes), Colibri int4-gs64 streaming container, 195.8 GB
command: make -C c glm53 (coordinator and workers); workers: EXPERT_WORKER=1 CLUSTER_WORKER_PORT=9100 GLM53_EXPERT_GB=<10|6.7> OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 ./glm53 (SNAP=<model>); coordinator: GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK=<128|256> OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 COLI_CLUSTER_WEIGHTS=52,48 CLUSTER_WORKERS=<worker-a>:9100,<worker-b>:9100 GLM53_VERBOSE=2 ./glm53 --model <model> --prompt "$(cat prompt.txt)" --greedy 1; tok_s = 245 / (prefill seconds printed on stderr); arms alternated 128,256 after one warmup at 256

hardware.cpu: coordinator Intel i5-8500 (6C/6T); two expert workers Intel i5-4570 (4C/4T)
hardware.ram: coordinator 31 GB DDR4; workers 15 GB each
hardware.storage: model on local SATA SSDs, ext4: coordinator Patriot P3 1 TB (~144 MB/s), workers ADATA SU650 (~371 MiB/s probe) and KingFast (~505 MiB/s probe)
hardware.os: coordinator Linux 7.1.13-hardened, gcc 16.2.1; workers Linux 7.1.8-arch / Ubuntu 26.04, worker binaries built with gcc 16 -march=native (Haswell); Tailscale TCP between hosts; background miners STOPPED on all hosts for the run, tailscaled at nice -5, engines at nice 0
